impactRating.rationale: Failure to use automated mechanisms to employ replay-resistant authentication exposes the tenant to: Inability to maintain individual accountability, Improper assignment of privileged functions, Privilege escalation.

portal.path: Entra admin center > Protection > Conditional Access

remediation.notes: Create a CA policy: Target admin roles > Grant > Require authentication strength > Phishing-resistant MFA

checks.impact: Privileged accounts protected only by TOTP or push MFA are vulnerable to real-time AiTM session hijacking. Attackers capture the post-MFA session token and have full authenticated access without the MFA device.
checks.rationale: Standard MFA (TOTP, push notification, SMS) is bypassed by AiTM phishing toolkits (e.g., Evilginx, Modlishka) that relay authentication in real time and capture session cookies. Phishing-resistant MFA (FIDO2, Windows Hello, certificate-based) is cryptographically bound to the origin and cannot be relayed by an attacker-controlled proxy.

impactRating.rationale: Failure to drive enrollment on stronger authentication methods leaves the user population overly dependent on phishable methods (SMS, voice) and increases susceptibility to AiTM proxy phishing, push bombing, and SIM-swap tradecraft.

portal.path: Entra admin center > Protection > Authentication methods > Registration campaign > Enable and target All Users

checks.impact: Users may remain on weaker methods (SMS, voice) indefinitely. This population is most exposed to SIM-swap, voice-channel interception, and AiTM proxy phishing. The control does not directly enforce strong methods — it nudges enrollment — so impact is gradual but measurable as a steady rise in strong-method adoption % over weeks. Pair with auth-strength CA policies for hard enforcement.
checks.rationale: The Microsoft Authenticator Registration Campaign nudges users registered with weaker authentication methods (SMS, voice, software OATH) to enroll Microsoft Authenticator with stronger options (push, passwordless, phishing-resistant). Without an active campaign, users tend to stay on whatever method they originally registered — leaving an avoidable gap that AiTM kits and push-bombing tradecraft exploit. Targeting 'All Users' ensures the nudge reaches every population, including long-stale registrations.

impactRating.rationale: Failure to ensure default authenticators are changed as part of account creation or system installation exposes the tenant to: Inability to maintain individual accountability, Improper assignment of privileged functions, Privilege escalation.

portal.path: Entra admin center > Identity > Hybrid management > Microsoft Entra Connect

remediation.notes: Verify Password Hash Sync status in Microsoft Entra Connect or Microsoft Entra Cloud Sync

checks.impact: On-premises credential compromises are invisible to Entra ID Identity Protection when password hashes are not synced. Stolen on-premises credentials used in cloud authentication generate no risk signal and are not blocked by risk-based CA policies.
checks.rationale: Password hash sync ensures that Entra ID has a copy of password hashes from on-premises AD. Without it, leaked on-premises credentials cannot be detected by Entra ID's Identity Protection and compromised on-premises accounts can authenticate to cloud services with no cloud-side risk signal.

Microsoft Learn — Risk detections in Microsoft Entra ID Protection

nist-800-53.title: Re-authentication

impactRating.rationale: Failure to terminate sessions after a defined period exposes the tenant to credential replay attacks — a reusable TAP intercepted during transit can be used by an attacker before it expires.

portal.path: Entra admin center > Protection > Authentication methods > Temporary Access Pass > Is usable once: Enabled

remediation.notes: This ensures each TAP is consumed on first use and cannot be replayed

checks.impact: An intercepted TAP can be used by the attacker for any authentication within the TAP's lifetime. The legitimate user's use of the TAP does not invalidate it, allowing concurrent attacker access.
checks.rationale: A multi-use TAP is valid until its expiry window regardless of how many times it is used. If a TAP is intercepted in transit (phishing, shoulder-surfing, insecure delivery channel) the attacker can use it repeatedly until expiry. Single-use TAPs limit the replay window to the first authentication.

references.title: Microsoft Learn — Configure Temporary Access Pass
Maester — EIDSCA.AT02 Temporary Access Pass single-use enforcement

cis-m365-v6.title: Ensure sign-in to shared mailboxes is blocked

nist-csf.title: Users, services, and hardware are authenticated; Access permissions, entitlements, and authorizations are defined in a policy, managed, enforced, and reviewed, and incorporate the principles of least privilege and separation of duties

impactRating.rationale: Failure to proactively govern account management of individual, group, system, service, application, guest and temporary accounts exposes the tenant to: Inability to maintain individual accountability, Improper assignment of privileged functions, Privilege escalation.

effort.overrideReason: Blocking direct sign-in to shared mailboxes breaks automation scripts, monitoring tools, and legacy service accounts that authenticate directly to shared mailboxes (rather than using delegate access). Service-scope disruption — end users accessing via delegation are unaffected, but integrations using direct auth break immediately.

portal.path: Entra admin center > Users > select shared mailbox user > Properties > Account enabled > No

remediation.notes: Block sign-in for shared mailbox accounts: Set-AzureADUser -ObjectId <UPN> -AccountEnabled $false

checks.impact: Shared mailboxes with active credentials can be accessed by anyone who knows the password, including former employees who had access before the mailbox was shared. These sign-ins may not appear in per-user audit logs.
checks.rationale: Shared mailboxes with enabled sign-in can be used with a username and password, bypassing the multi-user visibility of shared mailbox access. If credentials are set or remain from before the mailbox was converted, they may be used to authenticate without anyone noticing.

references.title: Microsoft Learn — About shared mailboxes
Microsoft Learn — Block sign-in for the shared mailbox account

cis-m365-v6.title: Ensure that SPF records are published for all Exchange Domains

nist-csf.title: The confidentiality, integrity, and availability of data-in-transit are protected

impactRating.rationale: Failure to proactively govern account management of individual, group, system, service, application, guest and temporary accounts exposes the tenant to: Inability to maintain individual accountability, Improper assignment of privileged functions, Privilege escalation.

effort.overrideReason: SPF is a single DNS record publish but overly restrictive records (hard fail) can cause mail delivery issues for legitimate senders using third-party services not yet in the SPF record. Risk is real but implementation is not inherently phased.

remediation.notes: Connect to Exchange Online and verify accepted domains

checks.impact: Attackers can send email appearing to come from your domain without SPF, DKIM, or DMARC to block them. Phishing campaigns impersonating your organization are more effective when the sending domain has no authentication.
checks.rationale: SPF (Sender Policy Framework) authorizes which mail servers may send email on behalf of your domain. Without an SPF record, receiving servers cannot verify that email from your domain is legitimate, enabling spoofing and reducing deliverability of legitimate email.

references.title: Microsoft Learn — Set up SPF to help prevent spoofing
RFC 7208 — Sender Policy Framework (SPF) for Authorizing Use of Domains in Email

portal.path: Entra admin center > Groups > New group > Membership type = Dynamic User > Rule: (user.userType -eq "Guest")

checks.impact: Without a guest dynamic group, guest users are not automatically included in access review cycles or guest-specific Conditional Access policies, creating governance gaps for external identities.

checks.impact: Security controls defined in the policy (MFA, device compliance, session limits) are not enforced for any user — the policy is a no-op. Since the policy still appears in the inventory as 'Enabled', it creates audit evidence that does not reflect actual protection.

impactRating.rationale: Failure to document, assess risk and approve or deny deviations to standardized configurations exposes the tenant to: Inability to maintain individual accountability, Improper assignment of privileged functions, Privilege escalation.

effort.overrideReason: Disabling per-user MFA (legacy MFA) while migrating to CA-based MFA is a high-risk operation if not sequenced carefully. If per-user MFA is disabled before CA-based MFA policies cover all users, affected users lose MFA protection entirely. Three phases: (1) ensure CA-based MFA policies cover all users in report-only, (2) validate CA coverage, (3) disable per-user MFA and switch CA to enforce. Complexity derivation underestimated because Medium severity doesn't trigger phased detection.

portal.path: Entra admin center > Users > Per-user MFA > Ensure all users show Disabled

remediation.notes: Use Conditional Access policies for MFA enforcement instead of per-user MFA

checks.impact: Per-user MFA and Conditional Access policies can conflict, resulting in double-MFA prompts or unexpected bypass scenarios. Users not covered by either mechanism may authenticate with password only.
checks.rationale: Per-user MFA is a legacy enforcement method that applies MFA independently of Conditional Access. It does not support modern features like risk-based enforcement, device trust, or named location exceptions. Running both per-user MFA and CA simultaneously creates conflicts and gaps.

references.title: Microsoft Learn — Enable per-user Microsoft Entra multifactor authentication to secure sign-in events

effort.overrideReason: Enabling a CA policy to block legacy authentication protocols (IMAP, POP3, basic auth SMTP) breaks mail clients and apps that have not migrated to modern auth. Two phases: report-only CA policy (identify legacy auth traffic via sign-in logs) → enforce blocking after legacy client remediation. checks.impact: Attackers can spray passwords against legacy protocol endpoints and authenticate successfully even when CA MFA policies are in place. A single compromised account via legacy auth gives full mailbox and Graph API access.
checks.rationale: Legacy authentication protocols (Basic Auth, NTLM over SMTP/IMAP/POP3) do not support MFA and cannot be evaluated by Conditional Access policies. Any user with legacy auth enabled is a viable target for password spray attacks that MFA cannot stop.

effort.overrideReason: Disabling weak authentication methods (SMS OTP, voice call) removes sign-in options for users who currently rely on them as their only registered MFA method. impactRating.rationale: Failure to configure systems to provide only essential capabilities by specifically prohibiting or restricting the use of ports, protocols, and/or services exposes the tenant to: Inability to maintain individual accountability, Improper assignment of privileged functions.

effort.overrideReason: Disabling SMTP AUTH is one of the most commonly underestimated M365 changes. Legacy printers, scanners, MFDs, LOB applications, and monitoring systems frequently use SMTP AUTH without IT's knowledge. Orgs routinely discover unknown senders only after enforcement. Two phases: SMTP AUTH audit via message trace (identify senders) → disable with per-mailbox re-enablement for verified legacy devices. Complexity was understated by derivation.

powershell.command: Set-TransportConfig -SmtpClientAuthenticationDisabled $true. Disable SMTP AUTH org-wide and enable per-mailbox only where required

checks.impact: Attackers can spray passwords against the SMTP AUTH endpoint to compromise mailboxes and use them as relay points for spam, phishing, or internal reconnaissance — all with only a valid username and password.
checks.rationale: SMTP AUTH is a legacy protocol that supports Basic Authentication and is used for sending email from devices and applications. If enabled globally, any client can attempt to authenticate to Exchange using only a username and password, bypassing all modern authentication controls.

cis-m365-v6.title: Ensure that DKIM is enabled for all Exchange Online Domains

impactRating.rationale: Failure to implement this control may expose the tenant to security risks.

effort.overrideReason: Enabling DKIM requires DNS record publication and Exchange Online activation per domain. Misconfiguration causes mail authentication failures. Two phases: configure signing → publish DNS records and validate.

remediation.notes: Connect to Exchange Online and verify accepted domains

checks.impact: Without DKIM, outbound mail from Exchange Online domains lacks cryptographic authentication. Receiving servers cannot distinguish legitimate mail from spoofed messages claiming the same domain, weakening DMARC enforcement and reducing deliverability scores. Phishing messages impersonating the domain are harder for recipients to detect.
checks.rationale: DKIM signs outbound messages with a domain-specific cryptographic key, allowing receiving servers to verify that mail was not tampered with in transit and genuinely originated from the domain. Without DKIM, spoofed messages claiming to be from the domain will pass unauthenticated and may deceive recipients.

checks.impact: Known vulnerabilities on managed devices go undetected and unremediated. Attackers who identify these devices via active scanning or from breach intelligence have an unpatched entry point.
checks.rationale: Vulnerability scanning surfaces known exploitable vulnerabilities in managed device software and OS configuration. Unpatched vulnerabilities are the primary initial access vector for ransomware and targeted attacks.

references.title: Microsoft Learn — Microsoft Defender Vulnerability Management

checks.name: Ensure MX records exist and point to Exchange Online for all email domains

impactRating.rationale: Failure to route email through Exchange Online mail flow exposes the tenant to: Security control bypass; mail not traversing Exchange Online skips ATP scanning, DLP policies, mail flow rules, and anti-phishing defenses.
